review.scope: Only unexecuted proposal edits and evidence clarifications. No actual driver, original approved spec/status or failed execution artifact was edited; no SDK/payload rerun.

findings.evidence: The analysis trio was absent during review preparation. Complete and bind those artifacts before presenting; their final existence/hash checks are recorded in the sealed receipt.

Inherited PYTHONOPTIMIZE can remove assert gates. New outer and inner launches use a bound interpreter with -I -B; an explicit non-assert guard rejects optimize!=0 or isolated!=1. Pure guard and launch-wiring tests pass.

A numeric one-attempt field alone does not prevent replay/concurrency. Add atomic exclusive per-approval claim, keep it consumed on failure, exclude ledger from cleanup. Duplicate/race tests pass; external ledger deletion remains outside the guarantee.

Status/index hashes do not reveal all hidden-worktree flags. Prospective adapter rejects lowercase assume-unchanged and S skip-worktree tags in every repository. Actual prior run did not record this flag check; no retrospective claim.

A same-path untracked edit need not change status text. Rehash every bound recording file and actual approval immediately before launch and after return; same-path mutation test passes. These are point-in-time checks, not continuous filesystem attestation.

Post-run-only audit is incomplete on launch errors or interruption. New prelaunch record, explicit exception/signal handling, bounded child termination and best-effort finalization preserve actual partial outcomes. SIGKILL can still truncate final records and is disclosed.
Inherited PATH could select a different inner Python. Use sys.executable from the hash-bound canonical outer interpreter; both launches are isolated. Structural launch test passes.

The prior root-rebind approval was bound but not separately copied. Add prior-root-rebind-approval.json to the prospective adapter artifacts; previous actual failure capsule already retains its own original approval copies unchanged.

Offsets held only in memory could be lost if Popen fails. Four-line proposed repair now writes a prelaunch JSON record after successful seek/reset and before Popen. A failed seek may still leave only the driver error trace; no unobserved offset is invented.

Root/authorization guard rejection lacked executable verification. Thirteen pure tests now exercise valid/invalid root states, flags, Python mode, same-path byte drift, duplicate/concurrent claims, unsafe claim path and guard-to-launch wiring, without Git mutation or target processes.

Add an explicit reproducible partial-failure sealing procedure: exact inputs/destinations, no overwrite, inventory boundaries, certificate-content exclusions, manifest/archive verification, receipt facts and retention/cleanup. No actual retry sealing result is fabricated.
Same optimization defect as blind-2, independently traced. Bound -I -B and explicit runtime-mode rejection added; tests cover rejected optimized/nonisolated states.
Same replay/concurrency defect as blind-3. Exclusive claim added before materialization/SDK; consumed claims retained and duplicate/race tests pass.
Same status-versus-byte gap as blind-5. Repeated recording/approval byte checks added immediately before launch and after completion, with retained snapshot checks.

Pre-verified regression gap: allowing an extra untracked path could reach the downstream snapshot equality gate. Pure checker rejects that exact fixture; static wiring verifies it is called before claim and Popen. Test remains under qualification artifacts, without unauthorized scripts/tests or CI production edits.
